newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says recovery on track after GDP slips.
newsitem.headline: Japan says recovery on track after GDP slips.

text.p: Japan said on Friday its economic recovery was on track despite figures showing the economy shrank in the three months to June after strong growth in the previous quarter.

The Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said gross domestic product (GDP) -- a key gauge of the economy's health -- fell a real 0.7 percent in the April-June period from the previous quarter. This would translate into a drop of 2.9 percent on an annualised basis.
The EPA declared immediately after releasing the figures that no additional budget to stimulate the economy would be needed, as many have demanded.
Taking first half-year figures showing annualised growth of 6.4 percent, it said Japan's "moderate recovery" was on track.
GDP measures the country's output of goods and services minus net income from overseas production.
Jesper Koll, head of research at J.P. Morgan, said: "I think that basically all is well with the Japanese economy. Private sector demand is taking over as the engine for growth."
Mikihiro Matsuoka, senior economist at Daiwa Institute of Research, told Reuters: "These numbers are within expectations, so there will be no change in the response of the markets."
Economists polled by Reuters had estimated an average fall of 1.1 percent in the April-June period quarter-on-quarter, with the forecasts ranging between a drop of 0.3 and 1.8 percent.
The government declared in February that the economy was gradually recovering after four years of negligible growth. But recent economic data have shown that the recovery was not gaining momentum.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has said he would like to look at the GDP data before deciding the date of the general elections and whether to draw up an extra budget with economic stimulus steps.
